name: Battery C, 62nd Coast Artillery (AA) / 62nd AAA Gun Bn
note: 1st Bn, 62nd CA (AA) became the 62nd AAA Gun Bn at Palermo; the battery's own reports switch name between Mar and Apr 1944.

name: Battery D, 106th AAA AW Bn (SP)
note: Kentucky National Guard (106th CA Bn (AA), Separate, until 1943). Its battalion's dated attachments to the 45th Infantry Division are in relations.csv (etoob-45ID/p180).

name: Medical Detachment, 67th Coast Artillery (AA) / 894th AAA AW Bn
note: The regiment's medical detachment: a regimental section with the Regimental HQ Battery and a section for each battalion, its men on special duty with the batteries. 2nd Bn, 67th CA (AA) became the 894th AAA AW Bn; the detachment reports as the 894th's by 19 Mar 1944. Its 1942-43 reports are book-type (roll 794, parts 2-3); March-April 1943 are missing.

name: Medical Detachment, 113th Infantry
note: New Jersey National Guard, inducted 16 Sep 1940 with the 44th Infantry Division. From December 1941 on coastal defense (the reports call the regiment RCT 113). The detachment's book-type reports (roll 1690, parts 2-3) give the station of its headquarters; it also had sections with the battalions, so a man's own post may differ.

name: Company G, 113th Infantry
note: 2nd Battalion, 113th Infantry: beach patrol on the Delaware coast (Bethany and Rehoboth Beaches) in 1943, then Port Republic, N.J., Fort Dix and Camp Pickett, Va. In April 1944 the company sent 16 of its NCOs and men as overseas replacements.

name: Company B, 313th Infantry (79th Infantry Division)
note: Its reports: Crown Hill Camp, Plymouth, 11-12 June 1944; aboard ship 13 June; Sébeville (inland from Utah Beach) 14 June; the drive on Cherbourg, which fell on 26 June; then south to the Ay river and the battle for La Haye-du-Puits in July. Stations give the nearest hamlet and a grid reference on the French Lambert Zone I grid, with a distance and bearing from the grid point.

name: HQ Battery, 128th AAA Gun Bn (Mbl)
note: A 90 mm gun battalion activated at Fort Bliss, Texas, on 20 May 1943. Third Army, as an army or corps battalion, from Normandy (late June 1944) to May 1945. Its headquarters ran the SCR-584 radar and the communications net. For 1945 the positions are the battalion's symbol on Third Army's antiaircraft situation maps.

name: 9th Armored Division
note: Activated 15 Jul 1942 at Fort Riley. The positions are the division's (or a combat command's), from its 1945 G.I. Stories booklet, Third Army's after action report and other division-level sources, and are drawn as assumed.

name: Headquarters, 9th Armored Division (command post)
note: The division's command post, from the ETO order of battle's table of command posts (etoob-9AD/p503-505). A headquarters' own position: not the division's units, which were spread around it (the 60th Armored Infantry Bn at Metzeresche while the command post was at Ennery). Transcribed from 31 Jul 1944 to 6 May 1945: the whole table.

name: 60th Armored Infantry Battalion (9th Armored Division)
note: Part of the 9th Armored Division (etoob-9AD/p499). The positions are the battalion's own, from its monthly after action reports, October 1944 - March 1945, as transcribed by EUCMH (eucmh60aib; original in NARA RG 407), and are drawn solid. A company's move (Able Co to Distroff, 9 Feb 1945) is not the battalion's and is not a station. Transcribed so far: October 1944 - March 1945.

name: Headquarters, 45th Infantry Division (command post)
note: The division's command post, from the ETO order of battle's table of command posts (etoob-45ID/p184-187). A headquarters' own position: not the division's units, which were spread around it. Transcribed from 15 Aug 1944 to 1 May 1945: the whole table.

name: Headquarters & Headquarters Battery, 1st Bn, 62nd Coast Artillery (AA)
note: Book-type reports, Nov 1942 - Jun 1943 (roll 782 part 1, rg64-427178735); March 1943 is not filmed (a missing-date slip, p0664). Its moves are Battery C's: Châteaudun 27 Feb, Algiers end of April, Ferryville 20 June.

name: Headquarters & Headquarters Battery, 2nd Bn, 62nd Coast Artillery (AA)
note: Book-type reports Oct 1942 - Jun 1943, daily forms in July 1943 (roll 782 part 2, rg64-427179736). Sailed on the Uruguay; at Oran Nov 1942 - Feb 1943, then Telergma (Merrit Air Field), Châteaudun, Berteaux, Ferryville and Sicily.

name: Headquarters & Headquarters Battery, 3rd Bn, 62nd Coast Artillery (AA)
note: Book-type reports Nov 1942 - Jun 1943 (roll 782 part 2, rg64-427179736, from about p0660). The unit's name is read on the scan from April 1943 (p0747); for Nov 1942 - Mar 1943 it is from the OCR of the forms, and the pages are taken as this battery's by their place on the roll.

name: Battery A, 62nd Coast Artillery (AA)
note: A 90 mm gun battery (its May 1943 reports). Book-type reports Sep 1942 - Jun 1943 and daily forms in July 1943 (roll 782 part 3, rg64-427180737). Crossed on the Argentina with Battery C.

name: Battery B, 62nd Coast Artillery (AA)
note: A 90 mm gun battery (its own reports). Book-type reports (roll 782 part 4, rg64-427181738); from February to May 1943 they seldom name a place, so much of that spring is not on the map.

name: Battery D, 62nd Coast Artillery (AA)
note: Only July 1943 is filmed in this series so far as found (roll 783 part 1, rg64-427182819, about p0598-p0665); its Nov 1942 - Jun 1943 reports have not been found.

name: Battery E, 62nd Coast Artillery (AA)
note: Only July 1943 is filmed in this series so far as found (roll 783 part 1, rg64-427182819, from about p0666).

name: Battery G, 62nd Coast Artillery (AA)
note: An automatic-weapons battery. Book-type reports Nov 1942 - Jun 1943 (roll 783 part 2, rg64-427183820). Crossed on the Dunnottar Castle; defended Mers-el-Kébir, then the fighter airfield at Châteaudun-du-Rhumel (Feb - May 1943) and Telergma's airfield (June).

name: Medical Detachment, 62nd Coast Artillery (AA)
note: The regiment's medical detachment: a headquarters section and aid station and a section for each battalion, with aid men in the batteries. Book-type reports Nov 1942 - Jun 1943 (roll 783 part 4, rg64-427185822). These rows follow the detachment's headquarters; the notes say where the sections went with their battalions.

name: Battery H, 62nd Coast Artillery (AA)
note: An automatic-weapons battery (8 guns; inferred from the lettering). Book-type reports Nov 1942 - Jun 1943 (roll 783 part 3, rg64-427184821). Sailed from Glasgow in the Strathaird on 26 Dec 1942 and landed at Algiers in the first days of January 1943, after the rest of the regiment; defended Algiers and Maison Carrée, then an airfield the reports call Louisiana Airbase (Mar - May 1943), then the Ferryville sector.

name: Battery F, 62nd Coast Artillery (AA)
note: July 1943 only in this series (roll 783 part 1, rg64-427182819). By Lake Bizerte, then Bizerte, LST 314, Porto Empedocle and Palermo.

name: Battery I, 62nd Coast Artillery (AA)
note: July 1943 only in this series (roll 783 part 3, rg64-427184821). By Lake Bizerte, then Bizerte.

name: Battery K, 62nd Coast Artillery (AA)
note: July 1943 only in this series (roll 783 part 3, rg64-427184821). By Lake Bizerte, then the loading area at Bizerte.

name: Headquarters & Headquarters Battery, 2nd Bn, 67th Coast Artillery (AA) / 894th AAA AW Bn
note: Daily forms Oct 1943 - Mar 1944 read on the scans (rolls 454453373, 456842549, 459806357, 461579515, 463960255, 466429103). Named places and move mileages only, no grid references. Redesignated HQ HQ Btry, 894th AAA(AW) Bn, effective 20 Mar 1944, by G.O. 42, HQ Fifth Army, 14 Mar 1944 (rg64-466429103/p0781). The regiment's Medical Detachment's men with the battalion were attached to this battery for rations and quarters (e.g. rg64-461579515/p0950, rg64-466429103/p0774).

name: Battery E, 67th Coast Artillery (AA) / Battery A, 894th AAA AW Bn
note: 2nd Bn, 67th CA (AA). Daily forms 1 Jan - 20 Mar 1944 read for stations (rolls 461580516, 463960255, 466429103; heads and the move entries on the scan, other backs screened by OCR). Giving AA protection to the 1st Bn, 178th FA, 17 Jan - 26 Feb 1944. Redesignated Battery A, 894th AAA (AW) Bn, effective 20 Mar 1944, by G.O. 42, HQ Fifth Army, 14 Mar 1944 (rg64-466429103/p0966).

name: Battery H, 67th Coast Artillery (AA) / Battery D, 894th AAA AW Bn
note: 2nd Bn, 67th CA (AA). Daily forms 13 Jan - 20 Mar 1944 read on the scans (rolls 461580516, 463960255, 463961256, 466430104); 1-12 Jan and 1-3 Feb not read. Giving AA protection to field artillery (not named). Redesignated Battery D, 894th AAA (AW) Bn, effective 20 Mar 1944, by G.O. 42, HQ Fifth Army, 14 Mar 1944 (rg64-466430104/p0152).

name: Battery F, 67th Coast Artillery (AA) / Battery B, 894th AAA AW Bn
note: 2nd Bn, 67th CA (AA). Daily forms 1 Jan - 20 Mar 1944 read for stations (rolls 461580516, 463960255, 466429103, 466430104; station changes and move entries on the scan, other backs screened by OCR). Redesignated Battery B, 894th AAA (AW) Bn, effective 20 Mar 1944, by G.O. 42, HQ Fifth Army, 14 Mar 1944 (rg64-466430104/p0028).

name: Battery G, 67th Coast Artillery (AA) / Battery C, 894th AAA AW Bn
note: 2nd Bn, 67th CA (AA). Daily forms 1 Jan - 20 Mar 1944 read for stations (rolls 461580516, 463960255, 466430104; station changes and move entries on the scan, other backs screened by OCR). Redesignated Battery C, 894th AAA (AW) Bn, effective 20 Mar 1944, by G.O. 42, HQ Fifth Army, 14 Mar 1944 (rg64-466430104/p0094).
